clue.text: Literary set in a punt on river in opium dream

indicators.note: in an across clue, a punt on the river means the bet is written after the river's name

parts.note: Alph is the sacred river in Coleridge's Kubla Khan, a poem said to come from an opium dream
taken as written
a punt is a gamble, a bet

explanation.surface: A literary circle drifting in a punt along a river, lost in a drug-fuelled reverie.
explanation.walkthrough: Coleridge claimed Kubla Khan came to him in an opium-induced sleep; its river is Alph.
explanation.definitionFit: The letters of writing form a complete collection, so the set of letters used in literature is a cryptic description of the word.

clue.text: Large part of day filled with a ferment

indicators.note: the time of day is filled with the letter, so it goes inside

parts.note: evening is the later part of the day
taken as written

explanation.surface: A large part of the day spent full of agitation and excitement.
explanation.definitionFit: A leavening is an agent such as yeast that makes dough rise, which is what a ferment does.

clue.text: Often visited relative man had welcomed

indicators.note: the man's contraction welcomes the relative into its middle

parts.note: he'd is the contraction of he had
an aunt is a relative

explanation.surface: A man who had warmly received a relative on a visit.
explanation.definitionFit: A place that is haunted is one frequented, as a ghost or a regular customer frequents a favourite spot.

clue.text: Disaster, taking on black bear

indicators.note: the disaster takes on the colour at its front, so black's letter comes first

parts.note: a ruin is a disaster or downfall

explanation.surface: A catastrophe involving a black bear.
explanation.definitionFit: Bruin is the traditional folk-tale name for a bear, used as a general word for one.

clue.text: This is the end of many inflammatory diseases

definitions.text: This is the end of many inflammatory diseases

parts.note: read as a statement about a final stage, as though an illness is ending
read literally, it points at the closing letters of the names of illnesses ending in -itis

explanation.walkthrough: Arthritis, tonsillitis and bronchitis all end in the same three letters; those letters also spell the old contraction of 'it is'.
explanation.definitionFit: The suffix for inflammation closes words like arthritis, and its last three letters form the poetic contraction for it is.

clue.text: Part of wall fitted with extra breadth: that's hard to understand

indicators.note: the wall section is fitted with an extra letter placed inside it

parts.note: a gable is the triangular upper part of a wall under a pitched roof

explanation.surface: A builder's gable fitted with extra width, which is a puzzling piece of construction.
explanation.definitionFit: Gabble is rapid, garbled speech, the kind that a listener struggles to follow.

clue.text: Grazing animal left in splendid meadows

indicators.note: the animal and the letter for left are placed in the word for splendid

parts.note: grand means splendid or magnificent
an ass, or donkey, grazes

explanation.surface: A donkey off to the left, grazing in fine meadows.
explanation.definitionFit: Grassland is open land covered with grass, which is what meadows are; a collective noun for them.

clue.text: Torment is base and wicked

parts.note: a bed is a base, as in a bed of concrete or a riverbed
evil means wicked

explanation.surface: Torment is a low and wicked thing to inflict.
explanation.definitionFit: To bedevil is to plague or harass someone persistently, a synonym for torment as a verb.

clue.text: After breather, energy to spring forward

indicators.note: energy's letter comes after the organ for breathing

parts.note: a lung is what one breathes with

explanation.surface: After catching breath, an athlete finds the energy to leap ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: A lunge is a sudden forward thrust of the body, as a fencer springs forward to attack.

clue.text: British sailor returning to port

indicators.note: the combination for British and sailor heads back, read in reverse

parts.note: UK, the United Kingdom
AB is an able-bodied seaman

explanation.surface: A British sailor heading back to harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: Baku, the capital of Azerbaijan, is a major harbour city on the Caspian Sea.

clue.text: Well-informed deputy, good and honest

parts.note: to be up on something is to be well informed about it
a stand-in deputises for someone

explanation.surface: Praise for a knowledgeable deputy who is decent and honest.
explanation.definitionFit: An upstanding person is upright and respectable, of good character and trustworthy.

clue.text: Boxes, and gets involved in conflict on playing field

indicators.note: in an across clue, the conflict word sits on the playing field, so it follows it

parts.note: a rec is a recreation ground, a public playing field
to tangle with someone is to get into a fight with them

explanation.surface: Someone who boxes and gets into scraps on the sports ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boxes' reads as a verb for fighting, but the definition is the plural noun for shapes.
explanation.definitionFit: Rectangles are four-sided figures with right angles, the shape of most boxes drawn on paper.

clue.text: Induced to admit philosopher in courses

indicators.note: the past tense of lead lets the thinker in, holding him inside

parts.note: led means induced or persuaded
A. J. Ayer was a British philosopher

explanation.surface: A philosopher persuaded to join some courses of study.
explanation.definitionFit: Layered describes something arranged in strata, and a course is a layer of bricks or stone.

clue.text: Watch weight, facing contest

indicators.note: the weight's letter faces the contest word, standing at its end

parts.note: to vie is to contest or compete

explanation.surface: Advice to keep an eye on one's weight before a competition.
explanation.definitionFit: To view something is to watch or look at it, a plain synonym for the verb.

clue.text: Powerful leader rigged the odds going to bust criminal

indicators.note: the remaining letters burst into the middle of the villain

parts.note: a baddy is a villain or criminal

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters of the word are dropped, leaving the even ones

parts.note: the even-numbered letters of this word survive once its odd ones go

explanation.surface: A race fixer rigging odds before police raid a crook's den.
explanation.definitionFit: A big daddy is the most important or powerful figure, the boss of an organisation.

clue.text: Turning over papers, a judge giving mark

indicators.note: in a down clue the papers are flipped, read upwards

parts.note: ID, identity papers
taken as written
a critic judges works

explanation.surface: A judge leafing through papers before awarding a grade.
explanation.definitionFit: A diacritic is a sign such as an accent or cedilla added to a letter.

clue.text: Most skilful answer? Lucky

parts.note: blest, an old spelling of blessed, means fortunate

explanation.surface: A quiz question about who is most skilful, answered by saying it was luck.
explanation.definitionFit: Ablest is the superlative of able, so the most capable or talented.

clue.text: Something you can't touch landed in boat

indicators.note: the word for landed goes in the flat-bottomed boat

parts.note: a scow is a flat-bottomed boat
acred means owning land, possessing acres

explanation.surface: An untouchable cargo brought ashore in a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A sacred cow is an idea or institution held to be above criticism, beyond challenge.

clue.text: As a woman, I am surprised to be holding a gun

indicators.note: the exclamation holds the weapon inside it

parts.note: aha is the cry of someone surprised
gat is slang for a gun

explanation.surface: A woman startled to discover she is carrying a weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: Agatha is a woman's first name, as in the crime novelist Christie.

clue.text: One slightly adjusting tea, we hear, with extra milk?

indicators.note: the letter is said like the drink, so we judge by ear

parts.note: the drink's name is said exactly like the letter
tea with more milk added is weaker; the question mark flags the loose sense

explanation.surface: Someone fiddling with their cuppa, wondering if it needs more milk.
explanation.definitionFit: A tweaker is someone who makes small fine adjustments, a tweak being a minor change.

clue.text: Removal of free social event

parts.note: to rid is to free of something
a dance is a social gathering

explanation.surface: Getting rid of a free social function.
explanation.definitionFit: Riddance is the act of getting rid of something, its disposal or removal.

clue.text: A greenish-yellow colour, but endlessly eloquent in a party

indicators.note: the shortened word sits in the party

parts.note: A DO, a do being a party

indicators.note: the final letter of the word is cut off

parts.note: vocal means outspoken or articulate

explanation.surface: A dress in a greenish-yellow shade, worn by someone who talks endlessly at a party.
explanation.definitionFit: Avocado is a named shade taken from the flesh of the fruit, a pale green tinged with yellow.

clue.text: Drive to clean out, with no pressure

indicators.note: the cleansing word is left without the letter for pressure

parts.note: to purge is to cleanse or clear out

explanation.surface: A driving need to clear things out, done without stress.
explanation.definitionFit: An urge is an inner drive or strong impulse to do something.

clue.text: A piece of jewellery shortly turned up in Indian dish

indicators.note: in a down clue the whole lot is turned upwards, read from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the jewel word is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: a tiara is a jewelled headpiece

explanation.surface: A jewel accidentally discovered in a curry.
explanation.definitionFit: Raita is an Indian side dish of yogurt with cucumber or other vegetables.

clue.text: Dopey elder, sacked, given new job

indicators.note: the letters are thrown out and reshuffled, as a sacked worker is turned out

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A dim older employee fired, then hired elsewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sacked' reads as dismissed, which pairs nicely with the definition about a new job.
explanation.definitionFit: To be redeployed is to be moved to a different post or task, typically within the same organisation.

clue.text: Arrogant poke round university

indicators.note: the poking word goes round the letter for university

parts.note: a prod is a poke

explanation.surface: A haughty jab at a university.
explanation.definitionFit: Proud can mean haughty or self-important, having too high an opinion of oneself.

clue.text: Pass year with novel, not quite satisfactory

parts.note: a ticket is a pass for entry

indicators.note: the book is not quite complete, its last letter dropped

parts.note: a novel is a book

explanation.surface: Getting a pass for a year with a novel is not quite good enough.
explanation.walkthrough: Tickety-boo is old-fashioned British slang meaning fine or in good order.
explanation.definitionFit: Tickety-boo means in good order, all right, everything going as it should.

clue.text: A little music in the pub

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a short section of a musical score
second meaning: a place serving drinks

explanation.surface: A snatch of music played at the local.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a measure of music and a public house's drinking room.

clue.text: Discharge, old and bowed

parts.note: an arc is an electrical discharge across a gap

explanation.surface: An old discharge of electricity making something bend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bowed' looks like bent, but it is the musical direction for string players to use the bow.
explanation.definitionFit: Arco is the musical instruction to play with the bow rather than plucking strings.

clue.text: Material wonderful, almost sumptuous

parts.note: fab is short for fabulous

indicators.note: the word is almost complete, losing its last letter

parts.note: rich means lavish or sumptuous

explanation.surface: Praise for a gorgeous, luxurious material.
explanation.definitionFit: Fabric is cloth, the woven material garments are made from.

clue.text: Free to air, do we half listen to this?

indicators.note: the letters are set free to move into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: only half of the two-letter word is kept, its first letter

parts.note: the first of the word's two letters is the half that is kept

explanation.surface: A broadcast free to air: do we only half listen to it?
explanation.walkthrough: Radio Two is a BBC national radio station.
explanation.definitionFit: Radio Two is a BBC station, something one tunes in to hear, so the question works as a definition by example.
